input.quote: 5.3 Sublicenses. AbbVie shall have the right to grant sublicenses (or further rights of reference), through multiple tiers of Sublicensees, under the licenses and rights of reference granted in Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, to its Affiliates and other Persons; provided that any such sublicenses shall be consistent with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and AbbVie shall remain liable for its obligations under this Agreement and for the performance of all Sublicensees.
input.rationale: The grant meets the preferred position. (i) Affiliate/contractor coverage: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to "its Affiliates and other Persons" without Harpoon consent (only a post-execution copy), and Sections 5.4, 5.5 and 13.16 expressly permit use of Affiliates and Third Parties (distributors, co-promotion, performance of obligations), so contractors acting on our behalf are covered. (ii) No at-will revocability: Harpoon has no termination-for-convenience right; termination is limited to uncured material breach (Section 12.2, with a 90-day cure and a "remedy of last resort" limitation) and insolvency, while Section 12.3 gives AbbVie a unilateral at-will termination right in our favour. Section 5.1.3(c) makes the grants automatic on the License Option Exercise Closing Date, and Section 12.1.2 converts them to non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable on natural expiry. (iii) Transferability: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets, and binds the grant of rights on any successor of Harpoon. Noted but not flagged: the 5.1.1/5.1.2 pre-option licences are limited-purpose and co-exclusive, which is consistent with the option structure of the deal rather than a scope deficiency.
